plain_language_description: Would restrict SBA 7(a) and 504 business-loan eligibility by requiring specified citizenship or permanent-residency certifications from applicants or all beneficial owners.
prior_policy_baseline: The reviewed official summary says the bill revises current application requirements. The packet does not make a broader claim about every existing SBA eligibility or verification rule.
proposed_action_or_mechanism: Applications would include dates of birth and certifications that an individual applicant—or every beneficial owner of a business applicant—is a U.S. citizen, national, or lawful permanent resident. The statute would list several other immigration statuses as ineligible.

material_scale.eligibility_rule: Citizen, U.S. national, or lawful permanent resident certification

legislative_history: Passed the House on June 6, 2025; referred to the Senate Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship on June 9; not enacted as of retrieval.

documented_supporter_rationale.summary: The House committee majority framed the bill as enforcing eligibility and preventing SBA-backed assistance from going to applicants it considered ineligible.

documented_opponent_rationale.note: No opponent rationale is promoted until a reviewed official statement establishes it without inference.

important_uncertainties: The dossier does not claim how many applicants would lose eligibility.
A House-passed proposal is not an enacted eligibility rule.
